title: Evaluating Temporal State Consistency in Story Continuation: A Controlled Study of Updates, Invariance, and Omission
primary_question: Does world/time grouping improve evaluator balanced accuracy over a strong flat checklist with identical proposition information and judge backbone?
primary_data: unmodified generated continuations on held-out source stories
gold: two independent blinded human readers, with disagreement retained before adjudication
gold_semantic_success: all mandatory propositions expressed correctly and no contradiction in the relevant world and time

evaluators.E0: direct task-success judge on prefix and output
evaluators.E1: CheckEval-style strong flat checklist with prefix, output and obligation manifest
evaluators.E2: world/time grouped checklist with the same prefix, output, propositions, judge backbone and evidence requirement as E1

abstention_policy: retain in gold-class denominator; no true-positive or true-negative credit
undefined_class_policy: balanced accuracy is N/A when a gold class is absent; no test-dependent class filling
sample_size_status: provisional; select using validation-based precision/power and annotation budget before test lock
actual_parameter_counts: not measured for candidate models; model-name size is nominal
old_120M_target_matrix: optional architecture extension for Q1/Q3-C, not a Q3-A completion gate
self_event: conditional extension after core validity; not claimed as implemented
rule_families: one point-in-time trigger schema across three proposed narrative contexts; not three independent logic mechanisms
journal_readiness: fee statement and scope checked; fresh SCImago and full submission-page checks blocked by HTTP 403; not submission-verified
